title: claude usage limits
description: Record of claude:limits — fleet-wide Claude subscription usage, one shared key with no TTL, on the central Redis since the CD-7 relocation. Grandfathered shape (CD-3). A Redis HASH, not a JSON string: fields are the DECODED record and every value arrives off the wire as a string. Several writers on several hosts share this one key, so `updated_at` is the OBSERVATION time rather than the publish time and a writer must not publish over a fresher one — a live statusline always beats a poll. The headline set and the model-scoped set carry INDEPENDENT stamps on purpose: only an oauth poll can supply the scoped fields, so a shared stamp would let a statusline write make a frozen scoped gauge look fresh. Each writer publishes its own cadence (`expected_refresh_s`) and the reader greys a gauge once that gauge's own stamp is cadence + grace old, so no consumer needs to know which source wrote it.

five_hour_pct.description: Five-hour window utilisation; readers clamp to [0,100] and reject non-finite values

five_hour_resets_at.description: Unix seconds the five-hour window resets; 0 or absent = unknown. A source that does not know it leaves the previous value alone rather than writing 0

seven_day_resets_at.description: Unix seconds the seven-day window resets; 0 or absent = unknown

updated_at.description: Unix seconds of the OBSERVATION behind the headline fields, not of the write. This is the field a writer reads back before publishing, so it must never be advanced by a writer that did not also refresh the values beside it

expected_refresh_s.description: How long the headline writer expects between its own writes (statusline 60, poll 300). The reader adds its own grace; absent means a pre-cadence writer and a legacy fixed window

host.description: Host that made the observation; display and provenance only

source.description: Where the observation came from: a live statusline, the desktop app's plan-usage-history file, or the oauth usage endpoint. `file` carries percentages only and no reset stamps

ts.description: Publish time, stamped by the publisher wrapper (rules.md). Distinct from `updated_at`, which is when the numbers were observed

scoped_model.description: Display label of the model-scoped weekly window, e.g. "Fable". A display string with no stable id — render it, never match on it

scoped_pct.description: Scoped window utilisation. Half a scoped set (a percentage with no label, or the reverse) renders as no scoped gauge at all rather than an unlabelled one

scoped_resets_at.description: Unix seconds the scoped window resets; 0 or absent = unknown

scoped_active.description: 1 when the scoped window is the currently binding constraint

scoped_count.description: How many scoped windows the source reported. Only one has ever been observed; this records the day that changes

scoped_updated_at.description: Unix seconds of the scoped observation — its OWN stamp. Absent or 0 means stampless, which the reader treats as always stale rather than letting it borrow the headline's freshness

scoped_expected_refresh_s.description: Cadence of the scoped writer (poll 300); same greying rule as the headline
